text:
maria: ran an int4 quant + rotary headwise-evenodd patch on Orpheus-7B (converted from Qwen) this morning. latency looks fine (1.8x token time vs fp16) but long-context QA quality tanked — EM down ~6pt vs fp16. also seeing occasional special-token/id mis-emits. attaching quick results and command.

aj: can you paste the exact convert/quant command and the eval numbers? :eyes:

maria: 
```
python tools/convert_model.py --src qwen --dst orpheus --rotary-mode headwise_evenodd --quant int4 --calib 10k --vocab-shift 1 --out /tmp/orpheus7b-int4
```

maria: eval (4k context SQuAD-like subset):
- fp16 baseline: EM 78.4, F1 86.1
- int4 (no rotary patch): EM 77.0, F1 85.5
- int4 + headwise_evenodd: EM 72.1, F1 81.8
lm perplexity (small corpus): fp16 12.3 | int4 12.9 | int4+patch 15.6

samir: hmm. two suspects: (1) rotary scaling/headwise interleave mismatch for the patched implementation, which would disproportionately hurt long contexts; (2) vocab/id shift during conversion — if special tokens got moved, generation can be off-by-one and cause weird early-term behaviors.

maria: i inspected tokenizer.json — the conversion applied `--vocab-shift 1` to line up embedding rows to the src model. BOS id ends up at 1 in the converted vocab, while runtime expects 0. some sample generations show the model emitting token id 1 as if it's a real token which then shifts later tokens.

aj: can you paste a minimal gen diff (fp16 vs int4+patch) showing the failure case?

maria: example:
```
prompt: "Summarize the legal clause about data retention..."
fp16 out: "The clause states that data will be retained for up to 2 years and then destroyed."
int4+patch out: "The clause states that  will be retained for up to 2 years..."
```
notice the missing first content token in the int4+patch run — looks like an early token id got swallowed/shifted.

samir: also check the rotary phase vector application. headwise_evenodd assumes even/odd interleaving of cos/sin; if our convert step transposes headdim order (proj order change), the multiplication will scramble attention positions for long spans. we should run a tiny forward-state identity test: run 1 token incremental vs batch and compare kv_cache slices.

maria: good call. i'll bisect: runs = [quant-only, quant+vocabshift, quant+rotarypatch]. will dump `kv_cache[0][:8]` for a long prompt and diff.

eval-bot: automated run results attached:
- run-a (int4, no patch): EM 77.0 | F1 85.5 | ppl 12.9
- run-b (int4 + vocab_shift): EM 75.8 | F1 84.4 | ppl 13.7
- run-c (int4 + vocab_shift + headwise_evenodd): EM 72.1 | F1 81.8 | ppl 15.6
logs: gs://redwood-runs/4461239876/ (contains kv dumps and conversion metadata)

aj: if run-b is worse than run-a, vocab_shift already hurts. try remapping special token ids instead of shifting the whole vocab.

samir: :thumbsup: add an assert in convert_model.py that verifies special token ids (BOS, EOS, PAD, UNK) map to expected runtime ids, and add a unit test that compares kv_cache after one step between src and converted model on a small input.

maria: will do. next steps: (1) run the bisect and post diffs, (2) add convert asserts + unit test, (3) try headwise implementation with explicit headdim reorder to match proj order. TL;DR: int4 quant itself is ok; the big regression comes from vocab_shift + the headwise_evenodd rotary patch interacting on long contexts. pinging @aj @samir when bisect results are in. :thinking_face:
